question.text: A ball weighing 1 kg is held motionless, suspended by two strings OA and OB, with the geometry described below. Taking g = 10 m/s², work out the tension carried by each of the strings OA and OB.
conditions: ball hangs in equilibrium from strings OA and OB
string OA makes a 30° angle with the horizontal at its upper fixed point A
string OB makes a 60° angle with the horizontal at its upper fixed point B
at O, string OA makes a 120° angle with the downward vertical, string OB makes a 150° angle with the downward vertical, and OA and OB make a 90° angle with each other

figure.description: Two fixed points A and B lie on a common horizontal line, A to the left and B to the right. Point O lies below and between them. String OA connects O to A, sloping up and to the left, and makes a 30° angle with the horizontal line at A. String OB connects O to B, sloping up and to the right, and makes a 60° angle with the horizontal line at B. The ball hangs directly below O on a vertical string, its weight w = 10 N pulling straight down. At O, going around: the angle from string OA to the downward vertical is 120°, the angle from the downward vertical to string OB is 150°, and the angle between OA and OB (measured the other way, over the top) is 90°.

solution.approach: Use the three marked angles at O between the two strings and the weight to apply Lami's theorem for three forces meeting at a point.

steps.text: Let T1 be the tension in OA and T2 the tension in OB. Write Lami's theorem using, for each force, the angle between the other two forces: T1 is opposite the 150° angle between OB and the weight, T2 opposite the 120° angle between OA and the weight.
Solve for T1 using w = 10 N.

common_mistakes.text: Treating string OA alone as if it supported the full weight vertically gives T1 = w/sin30° = 20 N, ignoring the pull from string OB.
